Application Data.DESCRIPTION OF OPERATIONS: Acme Office Supplies, Inc. specializes in the distribution and retail of a wide range of office supplies and equipment, including stationery, furniture, and technology products. We operate a 10,000 square foot retail space filled with a variety of items catering to businesses and educational institutions. Our inventory is valued at approximately $450,000 and is protected by a professionally monitored alarm system. We also provide delivery services and basic repair services for certain equipment, adhering to best practices in operational standards. We source our products from reputable suppliers within the domestic market and have a strict policy against importing from regions known for quality control issues or geopolitical instability to minimize potential liabilities.

Final Reason: The business is rejected due to a violation of a specific underwriting exclusion related to the nature of their operations. Despite the application stating no involvement with hazardous materials, the underwriting guidelines may not accept businesses categorized under the SIC 5043 (Office Supplies & Equipment) due to higher risk associated with retail operations.
Underwriting Guidelines:
Industry-Specific Restrictions
To mitigate underwriting risk, the following restrictions apply
specifically to office supplies and equipment businesses:
• Alarm System Requirement: An operational, professionally monitored alarm system is
mandatory for businesses with inventory exceeding $500,000 to reduce theft and burglary
losses.
• Professional Liability Coverage: Repair service providers must maintain professional
liability (errors and omissions) coverage to address potential claims arising from faulty repairs
or service errors.
• Restriction on Sourcing from High-Risk Overseas Suppliers: Businesses sourcing
office equipment or supplies from countries with known quality control issues or geopolitical
instability (e.g., certain regions with frequent product recalls or counterfeit goods) will be
subject to additional scrutiny or declination. This restriction is critical because poor-quality
imports increase product liability exposure and claims frequency.
